text:
maya: noticed a ~35% dip in otel spans for model-serving-prod right at auto-scale. Grafana span-rate panel dropped and SLO noise increased. looks like trace info being lost somewhere during connection handoff.

dan: which component is in the hot path? redis proxy, LB, or the runtime client?

maya: it traces back to our redis-shard-proxy (go pool). sample log around the event: 

```
IN 14:02:57.123 maya-request id=abc123 method=HGET key=model:kv traceparent=00-4bf92f3577...-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
PROXY 14:02:57.124 -> shard-10.12.3.45:6379 headers=[]   <-- traceparent missing on forward
```

sam: that log is telling. proxy reuses pooled connections and doesn't attach request headers to the downstream call path. when we reuse a connection we lose per-request context unless we explicitly copy headers.

eli: Prom alert fired at 14:03: otel_span_rate_ratio < 0.7 for eu-west1. timeline matches HPA creating new pods.

maya: repro steps in staging: scale model-serving + replay production capture -> consistently see traceparent strip in proxy logs.

dan: quick checks: otel-collector could be reparenting spans if headers are stripped, or our sampling ends up inconsistent. need to instrument the proxy to emit a metric: "requests_with_traceparent_total" vs total.

sam: short-term fixes: 1) change proxy to always copy trace headers (traceparent, tracestate, x-redwood-trace) on every forwarded request instead of implicit behavior; 2) enable sticky connections for a short window during scale to avoid mid-trace hop.

maya: proposed action list: 
- sam: PR for header passthrough and unit/integration test to assert trace headers preserved
- dan: add runtime fallback to accept x-redwood-trace and map it to span context if present
- eli: add Grafana panel for percent of requests with traceparent and a temporary alert suppression window tied to scaling events
- ops: canary proxy rollout in eu-west1 then promote

eli: can we also add a Prom rule to suppress otel_span_rate alerts during a window where kubernetes_pod_created > 0? otherwise scheduled scaling will keep ringing the noise.

sam: pushed canary build to eu-west1 and added an integration test that hits proxy and asserts headers forwarded. will monitor span counts.

ops-bot: deploy-bot started rollout of proxy-canary/sha-abc123 to eu-west1 at 2026-03-18T14:28:30Z

dan: after canary is live, I'll flip collector to debug and trace the path: proxy -> runtime -> collector to make sure sampling decisions are stable. also verify our batcher isn't aggregating away the root.

maya: created tickets INF-879 (trace loss during scaling) and INF-880 (proxy header passthrough). priority: high. please keep updates here and paste canary metrics. :thumbsup:

eli: update 14:50: canary shows span retention back to baseline, percent with traceparent rose from 62% -> 99% in eu-west1 after header fix. leaving canary for 1h before global rollout.

sam: will open a follow-up to add a stress test that scales rapidly while replaying capture to prevent regressions.

maya: thanks team. long-term we should add a tracing-aware connection-pool impl or propagate context at the connection layer rather than per-request plumbing.
